bp.title: Inside the fly's brain
bp.lead: Your opponent is the wiring of a real fruit fly, mapped cell by cell under an electron microscope. Before every move the board is shown to it, the signal spreads through its neurons for ten steps, and the move is read out from the result. This page shows that happening.
bp.stat.readout: neurons the move is read from
bp.stage.title: What you are looking at
bp.stage.body: Each dot is one neuron, placed where its cell body really is. They light up as the signal reaches them: press play to watch the ten steps for the position on the board below. Drag to turn the brain, scroll to zoom.
bp.region.0: The optic lobes. The board enters here, through the neurons of the eye.
bp.region.1: Neurons carrying what the eyes saw into the brain.
bp.region.2: Where most of the combining happens: learning and memory centres, and everything in between.
bp.region.3: Descending and motor neurons, the ones that would move the fly's body.
bp.region.4: The fly's 'spinal cord', running into its thorax.
bp.region.5: Touch, taste, smell and the rest. Here they receive facts about the game: castling, check, material.
bp.how.title: How a move is made
bp.how.see.title: It sees
bp.how.see.body: The position becomes light on 23,720 eye neurons: which piece stands where, and which squares each side attacks.
bp.how.spread.title: The signal spreads
bp.how.spread.body: For ten steps each neuron passes activity along its real connections. Their wiring is the fly's; only their strengths were trained.
bp.how.read.title: Instinct is read out
bp.how.read.body: A small layer reads 8,266 neurons and turns them into how much the fly likes each move, and how good it thinks the position is.
bp.how.choose.title: It imagines and chooses
bp.how.choose.body: The Planner and Thinker repeat this for the positions after their best candidates and your replies, then play the move that turns out best.
bp.flow.body: The same recording, per region. A line means one region is driving another right now; the thicker and busier, the stronger. Red is inhibition, a brake rather than a push. Gold lines lead to the neurons the move is read from.
bp.thoughts.body: The moves the fly considered for its last decision. The bar is its instinct; the number is how good the move looked after imagining the replies (in pawns, from the fly's side).
bp.sees.body: The board as it arrives at the eyes, always from the fly's side: its pieces, yours, and the squares each side attacks. A few squares near the edges have no eye neurons of their own, so the fly only sees them indirectly.
bp.faq.title: Good to know
bp.faq.real.q: Is this a real fly brain?
bp.faq.real.a: The wiring is real: every neuron and connection comes from the MaleCNS scan of a male fruit fly. The activity is a simulation running on that wiring, not a recording from a living fly.
bp.faq.learned.a: The strength of each connection, a bias per neuron, how the board reaches the eyes, and the small readout. Who connects to whom was never changed.
bp.faq.strength.a: Like a club beginner: roughly 1030 to 1340 Elo depending on the brain and how long it may think, measured against a limited Stockfish.
bp.faq.learning.q: Does it learn from our games?
bp.faq.learning.a: No. The brain is fixed after training; your games only make it think, they do not change it.
retina.preview: The position on the board, as the fly's 23,720 visual neurons would receive it (14 channels per square). After its next thought, this shows what it actually saw.
level.rookie.name: Fly Rookie
level.rookie.description: The older fly-v4 brain on pure instinct: one pass through the connectome, no imagining.
level.scribe.name: Fly Scribe
level.scribe.description: The older fly-v4 brain imagining 3 candidates and 2 replies each. Its search plays as well as v6's.
level.elder.name: Fly Elder
level.elder.description: The older fly-v4 brain thinking in stages while time allows. Trained on less than half of v6's positions.
select.speech.rookie.0: First day on the board! Which way do the knights go again?
select.speech.rookie.1: My propeller hat makes me move faster. Probably.
select.speech.rookie.2: I'm version 4. Version 6 is my big sister.
select.speech.scribe.0: I write every plan on this scroll. It's getting long.
select.speech.scribe.1: Older, yes. But my planning scored the best of all. Look it up.
select.speech.scribe.2: Dear diary: today I shall castle kingside.
select.speech.elder.0: In my day we had only 6.5 million positions to learn from.
select.speech.elder.1: *adjusts monocle* Hmm. A classical opening, I presume.
select.speech.elder.2: Version 6 thinks it knows everything. Let's see.
